summary: Source-anchored research for Enterprise Advanced licensing economics. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Under the November 2024 Customer Agreement, a Server is a virtual machine or container storing data up to the RAM amount in its Order Form. Enterprise Advanced covers the number of Servers and purposes specified there, and each Server used by an application must be covered. (low confidence)

Percona’s April 14, 2025 analysis warns that Enterprise Advanced licensing costs grow with multi-node deployments and that moving back to Community Edition can be difficult because of feature dependencies and support expectations. This is a competing supplier’s qualitative analysis, not measured savings or a customer postmortem. (low confidence)

Ops Manager documentation distinguishes Production and Test/QA, each requiring one license per server, from Development, requiring none. An environment that end users might use is Production even if it also performs testing. This classification matters when assigning migration staging and rollback environments. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The November 2024 Customer Agreement defines Server as a data-storing VM or container bounded by RAM specified on the Order Form. It licenses the contracted Server count; it does not establish a universal per-core tariff. A customer’s August 2023 forum question independently reports a 256GB unit on its own order. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/legal/customer-agreement/november-2024 ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/for-mongodb-enterprise-advanced-subscriptions-the-unit-of-ram-for-a-server-is-up-to-256gb/238244

MHBE solicitation BPM044630, issued July 5, 2024, requested a 24-month Enterprise Advanced subscription described as per 256 GB of RAM with Government Support Tier II, covering July 19, 2024 through July 18, 2026. This is evidence of a specific RAM-denominated procurement specification, not a verified award price or universal tariff. (low confidence)

Under the November 2024 agreement, subscription payments are non-refundable and an Order Form cannot be terminated for convenience. Inference: decommissioning a source deployment does not itself guarantee a refund for its remaining subscription term; cutover savings depend on negotiated contract terms. (medium confidence)

Under that November 2024 agreement, the royalty-free Enterprise Software license covers internal evaluation and development. Testing, quality assurance and production require an Enterprise Advanced subscription; a migration rehearsal cannot simply be assumed to qualify as free development. (medium confidence)

Ops Manager also documents RAM Pool licensing: one license can cover any number of servers within the purchased aggregate RAM limit. Do not apply per-server counting to every contract without checking which entitlement the customer purchased. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

MongoDB's pricing page directs Enterprise Advanced buyers to sales (Contact Sales) and lists Enterprise Server, Ops Manager and Cloud Manager, and a commercial license among the bundle contents, together with consultant support. The page publishes no Enterprise Advanced price, so it does not establish a generally applicable migration license price. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/pricing.md

The November 2024 agreement requires each Server used by an application to have Enterprise Advanced coverage. Inference for cutover planning: check simultaneous source and destination counts against the Order Form before dual-running; the cited agreement supplies no blanket free migration-overlap allowance. Percona independently identifies multi-node deployments as a licensing cost driver. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/legal/customer-agreement/november-2024 ; https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-pricing-explained-what-youre-really-paying-for/

The archived Cloud Manager Backup Agreement grants paying backup subscribers rights limited to Enterprise backup functionality during the subscription term, with no additional license fee under that agreement. It does not grant other Enterprise features. This scopes the assumption that every deployment using an Enterprise binary necessarily needs the full Enterprise Advanced package. (low confidence)

MongoDB presents Enterprise Advanced as a self-managed package with Enterprise Server, Ops Manager and Cloud Manager, a commercial license and consultant support; Percona independently describes it as a subscription that gives official support, advanced security features and management tooling such as Ops Manager. Its economics therefore include more than a database binary. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/pricing.md ; https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-pricing-explained-what-youre-really-paying-for/

For migration budgeting, inventory source and destination coverage during overlap, including Test/QA environments, against the actual Order Form. The agreement requires every Server used by an application to be covered, and Servers are defined by the RAM stated on the Order Form. A customer's forum post describes buying a separate Enterprise Advanced subscription for QA/Test. This is an inference from the contractual counting rules. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/legal/customer-agreement/november-2024 ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/for-mongodb-enterprise-advanced-subscriptions-the-unit-of-ram-for-a-server-is-up-to-256gb/238244

Percona states that its MongoDB-compatible software can be used without a MongoDB Inc. license fee or a mandatory Percona support contract; its support is optional. This is the supplier’s alternative commercial model, not evidence of equivalent features, migration effort or total cost for a particular deployment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-04-14)
